$comment: REBUILT 2026-09-01, three times in one day, and the third pass is the one he read on his phone and
pushed back on. Read the weekday section first if you only read one.
EVERY NUMBER IN THIS COMMENT WAS COMPUTED, and the command is named beside it. A number in a
comment that nothing recomputes is a rumour.
WHAT THE WEEK IS. Four sessions, full body, flat, on his ruling: "lets do full body flat".
Session A   overhead press fresh, back squat heavy, row, lower back     5 blocks, 29 sets
Session B   pulldown fresh, RDL heavy, front squat, split squat, bench  5 blocks, 30 sets
Session C   split squat and bench fresh, row, lower back                4 blocks, 24 sets
Session D   back squat, RDL, overhead press, bench heavy                5 blocks, 27 sets
THEY ARE NOT CALLED MONDAY ANY MORE, AND HIS OWN LOG IS WHY. He said "still using weekdays as
names" and I should have checked before ever writing them: 26 of his last 36 logged sessions were
performed on a DIFFERENT weekday than the card they came from, and his training is spread almost
evenly across all seven days. The weekday names were fiction the whole time.
THE KEYS ARE STILL WEEKDAYS AND THAT IS A KNOWN, DELIBERATE INCONSISTENCY. `gym_set.day` holds
monday/tuesday/thursday/friday on hundreds of rows, `src/lib/gym/week.ts` maps the integrated week
and the never-more-than-three-in-a-row rule onto real weekdays, and conditioning.json assigns its
slots the same way. Renaming the keys is a migration across four surfaces and a history. Nothing he
READS says a weekday now, and the session he trains is whichever card he opens.
EVERY BLOCK IS LED BY A REAL LIFT, which is the second thing he pushed back on: "one leading with
calves and the other woth justa deadbugs and carries seems like not actual lifts", and "leading
with lumbar extension?". Four blocks had an accessory as their lead. The week holds exactly 17
station-holding lifts and exactly 17 accessories, so pairing them ONE TO ONE makes every block
compound-led and costs nothing at all: 102 working sets and 59 sets that own the clock, both
unchanged. The old shape wasted two leads by pairing the split squat with the bench press, which
forced two accessories into blocks of their own.
DEAD BUGS ARE GONE AND HANGING KNEE RAISES TOOK BOTH ABDOMINAL SLOTS, on his ruling: "if im doing
bb rows I rather do hanging knee raises than deadbugs might be a little more work for back but I
wont lay down". Both sit behind a barbell row, which is what he asked for, and it answers an open
question that had been sitting on the RDL since 2026-08-27. equipment.json now declares the rack
and the pull-up bar on top of it ADJACENT, quoting him, and keeps the earlier refusal visible
rather than deleting it: the bar had been refused because he once said that walk works "only when
the gym is not busy", and what he said then was about a walk, while this bar is on top of the
uprights of the rack he is already standing in. If the bar is taken, the swap list carries the dead
bug and the hollow hold, so a wrong "you can" costs a swap and not a session.
AND THE ABDOMINAL ATTRIBUTION WAS CHECKED BEFORE IT WAS LEANED ON, which is the lesson from four
hours earlier. `hanging-knee-raise` sat in the `anti-extension` group, whose jointAction is
"Resisting lumbar extension isometrically". That is what a dead bug does. A knee raise MOVES the
spine, and the variant carried an unconfirmed jointActionNote of its own. It is in a new
`trunk-flexion` group now, with cable-crunch, and the cue was rewritten to ask for the pelvic curl
at the top, because the abdominal credit depends on it: stop when the thighs are level and it is
hip work with the abdominals only holding on.
WHAT THE REBUILD FIXED. `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/gym-targets.mjs`. DIRECT sets:
sets of an exercise where the muscle is a prime mover of a joint action the exercise performs.
was    now
Spinal erectors              0      6     <- see below, it took a correction and a question
Adductors                    3      6
Rhomboids and mid traps      3      6
Front deltoids               3      6
Triceps                      3      6
Lats                         6      9
Calves                       9      6     <- paid for the four above
Abdominals and obliques      9      6     <- paid for the four above
ALL SIXTEEN MUSCLES CLEAR THE FLOOR and the lowest number anywhere is 6, which is 50% clear of the
floor of 4. Two muscles that were comfortably above came down to pay for it, and that trade is the
flat ruling doing its job: a week with nine sets of calf work and none at all for four other
muscles is not flat, it is the shape the old programme happened to have.
THE ERECTORS ARE THE STORY, AND THE PROGRAMME WAS NEVER WHAT WAS WRONG. The first version of this
rebuild gave them six sets of 45-degree back extension, because the catalogue listed them as a
PRIME MOVER of it. That would have been the only direct erector work this gym can produce. The
attribution carried a jointActionNote saying nobody had confirmed it, and it does not survive: with
the spine held flat the joint action performed is HIP extension, and the erectors hold the trunk
against a flexion moment without changing length. That is the same role they play in the squat, the
row and the Romanian deadlift, where this same catalogue calls them SECONDARY. His own logged name
for the exercise is "Glute-Biased Back Extension", the name for exactly that version.
So the claim was corrected rather than leaned on, the gate went RED on one muscle, and the fix was
put to him as a question instead of written into a number. He answered in six minutes: "if i need
to try a new version of the back extension fine". That is why `spinal-extension` exists.
`lumbar-extension` is the same frame with the opposite instruction, the hips still and the spine
moving, prescribed twice a week with NO LOAD, and its cue is a DRAFT until he reports back.
THE 45-DEGREE BACK EXTENSION IS NOT DELETED. It is the first swap option on both lumbar-extension
slots, on the SAME MACHINE, and its 13 logged sets and its 40-to-50 lb ladder are untouched. The
two histories are deliberately NOT merged: one frame, opposite instructions, loads that do not
carry over. THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS FILE PRESCRIBED IT BODYWEIGHT with a cue opening "START WITH NO
WEIGHT", which would have thrown that ladder away, while the catalogue note two lines above the
muscle list already read "Logged 13 sets at up to 50 lb".
ONE BLOCK A SESSION IS MARKED OPTIONAL AND EACH SAYS WHAT DROPPING IT COSTS. That tag is the
surviving half of the drop-order sentence he cut on 2026-08-27, and it answers notes #7 and #11,
where he ran out of time. An earlier version of this rebuild marked EVERY block main, which deleted
the tag from the whole week; scripts/probe-gym.js caught that on the screen. It is always the last
block, because that is the one he actually stops at, and it is always compound-led now. Nothing
here is free to skip: eleven of the sixteen muscles sit at exactly two slots, so each of the four
states the price in direct sets rather than implying there is none.
WHAT IT COSTS ON THE CLOCK, in the units he can check against his own watch.
prescribed sets per week      98 before  ->  110 now
sets that OWN THE CLOCK       53 before  ->   59 now
The second row is the real one. A block is a lead plus a partner that rides in the lead rest, and
`validate.mjs` refuses a pair where the partner does not fit in the gap the lead offers, computed
from sets, reps and rest. So only the lead sets add wall-clock time. At his measured 4.0 minutes
per logged set that is about 11% more, and his watch median of 70 minutes over the last 90 days
would become about 78. THAT IS AN EXTRAPOLATION FROM THE OLD PROGRAMME, not a measurement of this
one, and his watch is what settles it.
AND THERE IS NO FAT LEFT TO CUT. Eleven of the sixteen muscles sit at exactly two slots, so removing
any block drops one of them below the floor. The ONLY cut that costs nothing on the muscle axis is
the box jump, from five sets to three, which he has already ruled is not volume. After that the
lever is rest lengths, not blocks.
ORDER IS A STRENGTH VARIABLE AND NOT A SIZE VARIABLE. Nunes 2021 (PMID 32077380,
sources/pubmed-32077380.txt), eleven good-to-excellent studies: starting with the multi-joint
exercise favours strength in that exercise (ES 0.32, p = 0.034) and order has no effect on
hypertrophy (ES 0.03, p = 0.862). `scripts/gym-order.mjs` asserts every pattern gets a slot in the
first two blocks of some session. All six pass.
CHEST GETS THE FRESH SLOT IN SESSION C and leads its own block in B and D. That was his complaint
on 2026-08-31, "chest being at the end of the sesion mostly", and the fresh-slot gate only ever
asked for it to be EARLY, which a partner in block 1 satisfies. Chest and lats are the two muscles
in this catalogue that get no helper credit from anything at all, which is why both are expensive
to cover and why both used to sit at the bottom of the week.
PAIRING CAME LAST AND ONLY WHERE IT IS REAL, on his ruling: "i want the best program possible first
an then figure out how to superset it". The exercises and their doses were chosen against the floor
first, and the blocks were formed from them afterwards. Agonist-antagonist pairing is the evidenced
kind (Zhang 2025: more reps, SMD 0.68, no strength or size cost, about 37% time saved), same-muscle
pairing costs volume load (SMD -1.08), and `validate.mjs` refuses the second kind outright.
PRIMERS ARE NOT VOLUME, on his ruling: "5 set of 3 jumps does not wgiht the same or more than 3 sets
of sauts or bench press". They are counted separately on the card. They ARE counted by gym-targets
and gym-strength, which read the whole file, and that is a known inconsistency rather than a hidden
one: it flatters quads and glutes by eight sets and touches nothing else.
THE HEAVY REP RANGES ARE HIS OWN LOGGED ONES. Back squat 5 to 7, RDL 6 to 8. His words:
"I feel like we should stay where we are... Im more worried on keeping my form and maybe improving
on that than going heavier", and he knows the cost: "I also know that does gonna kind of hinder my
progression."
WHAT THE EVIDENCE SETTLES, so nobody re-derives it:
Floor 4 direct sets per muscle per week, 10+ for more mass (Iversen 2021, quoted in targets.json).
Multi-joint lifts first in a session (Nunes 2021, ES 0.32, p = 0.034 for strength, nothing for size).
Bilateral over unilateral: equal hypertrophy (ES -0.21, p = 0.57) and better time efficiency.
Frequency does not need chasing once volume is equated (Schoenfeld 2019; Grgic 2018 found no
significant strength effect in middle-aged and older adults, p = 0.093).
MUSCLE ATTRIBUTION IS ANATOMY AND NEVER A TRIAL FINDING. See the legend at the top of
movements.json and sources/NOTICE-PER-MUSCLE-FIGURES-BEFORE-2026-09-01.md. gym-targets refuses to
grade at all unless every group is tagged `anatomy` and states its `jointAction`. Do not quote a
per-muscle figure from any document dated 2026-08-30 or earlier without recomputing it.
THE GATES. Run `node scripts/verify.mjs` before pushing.
content/gym/validate.mjs        shape, stations, walking route, verbatim whyHere, block fit
scripts/gym-order.mjs           every pattern gets a fresh slot (Nunes)
scripts/gym-targets.mjs         every muscle gets 4 direct sets (Iversen)
scripts/gym-strength.mjs        Table 4 per priority lift, against a dated baseline
scripts/gym-coverage.mjs        below-minimum, strict pairings, unsourced, against a baseline
scripts/check-ladder.mjs        does maxing the rep range earn the next weight (needs Neon)
scripts/probe-gym.js            the only test that presses a button. It caught two of the three
self-inflicted bugs today, both invisible to every gate above
TWO OPEN QUESTIONS ARE LIVE ON THIS FILE, both from 2026-08-27 with their facts updated to this
week: the assisted dip against the overhead extension, and whether another member could use the
pull-up bar while he is under a loaded bar. The third, about hanging knee raises in the rest, he
answered on 2026-09-01 and it is gone. So is the fourth, about the back extension.
CONDITIONING IS NOT IN THIS FILE. It lives in conditioning.json. The swim follows the lift on the
same evening, which is the constraint that makes session length a prescription rather than a
preference.
REBALANCED 2026-09-02, and the reason is a number nobody had put next to another number.
His question: "why are we allowing muscles to be at 28 or 30-something when it does not make
sense? Shouldn't we be balancing everything ... or are we miscounting?"
NOTHING WAS BEING MISCOUNTED. The 0.5 for a synergist is Pelland's own convention with their own
worked example, box jumps were already excluded from the loaded column, and glutes read 28.5 for
one reason: 10 of the catalogue's 27 movement patterns touch them against 2 that touch chest.
Glutes ride free on every squat, hinge and lunge. Chest only ever gets what it is handed.
WHAT WAS WRONG WAS THE PROGRAMME, on two targets that agreed with each other and were both being
missed in the same direction:
R1, strength: 3 to 5 DIRECT sets per lift per week. Twice-weekly lifts were at 3 sets each,
which is 6. They are at 2 now, which is 4.
R2, size: the week ran five squat-pattern instances and two hinges on one day.
AND THE STUDY THAT DECIDES IT IS ALREADY IN THE EVIDENCE FILE. Roth 2023 (PMID 36114738), 38
trained males, six weeks at 30 kcal/kg, 5 sets per exercise against 3: no difference in lean-mass
preservation, p = 0.966. He is in a deficit at 103.7 kg. So volume above the minimum effective
dose does not buy retention, and the excess was pure time cost against R3, where his median
session completes about a third of what is prescribed.
THE RESULT: 110 prescribed sets a week became 79. Glutes 28.5 to 16.5, quads 21 to 14, erectors
21 to 13, all now intermediate efficiency rather than lower. Abdominals were the ONLY muscle below
the minimum effective dose, at 1.5 loaded, and are at 4.5 on a loadable cable crunch. Every muscle
clears 4 direct sets, which gym-targets.mjs gates.
GLUTES, QUADS AND ERECTORS STAY IN THE TEENS ON PURPOSE. Getting them to 10 would mean cutting a
squat or a hinge, and those sets ride along on lifts R1 needs. That is a consequence of anatomy
and of twice-weekly main lifts, not a defect to engineer away.
CHEST WENT 9 TO 12 AND THAT IS THE ONE PLACE THIS PASS ADDED VOLUME. Tuesday's third squat became
the barbell bench press, which he named directly and which the catalogue and equipment.json both
already had. Chest now runs four different exercises across the week (BB Bench Press, Chest Fly
Machine, DB Incline Press, Machine Chest Press) instead of one exercise three times.
NO EXERCISE NOW REPEATS IN CONSECUTIVE SESSIONS except the overhead press across the Friday to
Monday wrap, which is a main lift and which section 1 of the evidence file says earns twice a week.

monday.name: Session A
monday.title: Session A: press fresh, squat heavy

blocks.label: Power Primer

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.cue: THREE JUMPS A SET, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE SET. Not as many as you can: three, then stop and rest. This is the one exercise here where being tired makes it worse rather than better, because what you are training is how fast you leave the floor, and the fourth jump is always slower than the first. A slow jump is just a squat you did standing up. Five sets of three is fifteen jumps, and every one of them should feel like the first. HOW TO DO IT. Stand a forearm's length from the box. Swing the arms back, bend the knees about a quarter of the way, and jump ONTO the box. Land with both feet flat and knees bent, quietly. Then STEP down one foot at a time, never jump down. Success looks like: you hear almost nothing when you land, and you could hold the landing still for two seconds. If you land with a thud or stumble, the box is too high. If the third jump feels slower than the first, rest longer before the next set rather than pushing through.

alts.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
alts.cue: On the floor. Lie on your back, one heel planted close to your butt, the other leg lifted and held straight out. Push through the planted heel and lift your hips until your body is a straight line from knee to shoulder, then lower slowly. Success looks like: you feel it in the back of the planted thigh and the butt cheek, not in your lower back. If you feel your lower back, your hips went too high. 3x12 each side.

alts.name: Lateral Bound
alts.cue: THREE OR FOUR BOUNDS A SIDE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE SET. Not as many as you can. Same reason as the box jump on Monday: what you are training is how hard you can push off in one go, and a tired bound is a slow bound, which trains something else. More work means more SETS. HOW TO DO IT. Replaces the broad jump, which you swapped out every single time. This is the sideways explosive work you asked for. Stand on your LEFT leg. Push off it sideways and land on your RIGHT leg only, then FREEZE completely still for two seconds before going back. Land with the knee bent and pointing over your toes, never caving inward. Only jump as far as you can land and freeze. Success looks like: silent landing, no wobble, no second little hop to catch yourself. If you cannot freeze it, go shorter.

alts.name: Pogo Hops
alts.cue: Small fast bounces on the balls of your feet, stiff ankles. 3x15.

alts.name: Banded Lateral Walk
alts.cue: Fallback only, on a day the dumbbells are all taken. Band above the knees, half squat, step sideways keeping the band tight. 3x10/side.

alts.name: Banded Hip Abduction
alts.cue: Short band above the knees, seated on a bench. Push the knees apart against the band and hold two seconds at the widest point, then let them come back slowly. Success looks like: you feel it on the outside of the hip, above and behind the hip bone. 3x15.

alts.name: Clamshell
alts.cue: On your side, short band above the knees, knees bent 90. Open the top knee like a clam without letting your hips roll backwards. Success looks like: your top hip stays stacked over the bottom one. If you have to roll back to open further, you have gone as far as it goes. 3x15 each side.

blocks.why: Jumps first, while you are completely fresh, because what they train is how fast you leave the floor and a tired jump is a slow jump. Five sets of three is fifteen jumps, which is the same dose as the three sets of three a side on the other primer day: eighteen contacts. It is not volume and it does not count toward the set total on this card, on your own ruling that five sets of three jumps do not weigh the same as three sets of a real lift.

blocks.label: Overhead Press

exercises.name: Seated DB Overhead Press
exercises.cue: STANDING, not seated: that is the difference between this and the seated version in the alternatives, and it is why this needs no bench. Done second in the session from 2026-08-22, and the reason is in "Why this is here". Dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing forward. Squeeze your bum and tighten your stomach BEFORE you press, so your ribs do not flare and your lower back does not arch. Press straight up until the arms are locked out with the dumbbells over the middle of your head, not in front of your face. Lower under control to the shoulders. Success looks like: your ribs stay down and you can hold the lockout still for a second. If your back arches to start the rep, go lighter.

alts.name: Machine Shoulder Press
alts.cue: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height, not above your ears. Press up until your arms are straight without shrugging, and come back down slowly until the handles are level with your shoulders again. Stop the set when your lower back starts arching off the pad.

alts.name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Press
alts.cue: One knee down, the other foot forward, one dumbbell in the hand on the SAME side as the down knee. Press it straight overhead without letting your ribs flare or your body lean away. It is two exercises at once: a press, and your trunk refusing to bend sideways under a load held on one side. Lighter than the two-dumbbell version by a lot, and that is the point.

alts.name: Seated DB Overhead Press
alts.cue: Bench upright, back supported. Takes the lower back out of it entirely.

exercises.name: DB Lateral Lunge
exercises.cue: This is the sideways movement you asked for, and it is loaded on purpose: unweighted band walks were shown to do little. Hold one dumbbell at your chest. Step wide to the LEFT and sit back into that left hip, keeping the right leg straight with the foot flat. Both feet stay pointing forward the whole time. Push off the left foot to come back. You should feel a stretch on the inside of the straight leg and work in the bent leg's hip. Start with a light dumbbell and a small step, then widen the step before you add weight.
exercises.whyHere: The sideways lunge goes in the press rest because it is done with the legs and the press is done sitting down with the arms.

alts.name: Front Squat
alts.cue: Your second squat of the week, deliberately light. This is the technique fix: because the bar sits on the FRONT of your shoulders, your body is forced upright and depth gets easier, which is exactly what a back squat struggles with. Bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows driven forward and UP so the upper arms are near parallel to the floor. Let your fingertips just hook under the bar, the shoulders hold it, not the hands. Sit straight down, elbows stay high the whole time. If the elbows drop, the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: Cossack Squat
alts.cue: The deeper version. Same sideways sit, but let the straight leg's toes come up and go as low as you can. Bodyweight first, hold a dumbbell at the chest when it is easy. 3x6/side.

blocks.why: Pressing overhead is the only movement in the week where the front of the shoulder is the prime mover, so without it that muscle gets nothing but helper work off the horizontal pressing. It leads here so it gets one session where it is done fresh. The sideways lunge goes in the press rest because it is done with the legs and the press is done sitting down with the arms.

blocks.label: Main Lift: Back Squat

exercises.name: BB Back Squat
exercises.cue: The lift we are progressing. Stance slightly wider than your hips with the toes turned out a little. Breathe IN and hold it, tighten your stomach like you are about to be poked, then sit down between your feet until the crease of your hip is below the top of your knee. Knees push out over your second toe, they do not fall inward. Stand up and breathe out at the top. Take a fresh breath and re-tighten before EVERY rep, not just the first.

alts.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides. Put the top of your back foot on the bench, laces down. Your front foot should be far enough forward that at the bottom your front shin is straight up and down, not leaning forward over your toes. Lower until your back knee is close to the floor. Drive up through the FRONT heel. The back leg is a kickstand, it does not push.

alts.name: Front Squat
alts.cue: Your second squat of the week, deliberately light. This is the technique fix: because the bar sits on the FRONT of your shoulders, your body is forced upright and depth gets easier, which is exactly what a back squat struggles with. Bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows driven forward and UP so the upper arms are near parallel to the floor. Let your fingertips just hook under the bar, the shoulders hold it, not the hands. Sit straight down, elbows stay high the whole time. If the elbows drop, the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up. Stepping backward rather than forward keeps the load off the front knee.

alts.name: Walking Lunge
alts.cue: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.

alts.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
alts.cue: Same upright effect with a dumbbell held at the chest, and no wrist or elbow demand at all. The easiest way to feel a deep upright squat.

alts.name: Leg Press
alts.cue: Feet shoulder width on the platform. Lower until your knees are near your chest without your lower back rounding off the pad, then press. Use this on a day your back is tired.

exercises.name: DB Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. A dumbbell in each hand hanging at your sides, palms facing your thighs, a small bend kept in the elbows. Lift both arms out SIDEWAYS, not forward, until your hands are level with your shoulders and no higher. Lead with the elbows, as if you were pouring from two jugs. Lower slowly, about twice as long coming down as going up. Success looks like: your shoulders do not rise toward your ears, and you can stop the weight dead at the top instead of it swinging. If either fails, go lighter. This is the SIDE of the shoulder, and it is the one thing nothing else in the week trains: every press works the front, every row works the back. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.
exercises.whyHere: The lateral raise goes in the squat rest because the shoulder takes no part in a squat, so it costs no extra time.

alts.name: KB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same movement with the lightest kettlebells, held by the handle. Use them if the light dumbbells are gone.

alts.name: Seated DB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same raise, sitting on the end of a bench. Sitting stops you swinging, so use it if the standing version keeps turning into a heave.

blocks.why: The heaviest thing you lift all week. Nunes 2021, eleven studies: strength gains are largest in whatever is performed at the beginning of a session, and order does nothing at all for size. Five to seven reps, because those are the rep counts you actually perform on this lift. The lateral raise goes in the squat rest because the shoulder takes no part in a squat, so it costs no extra time.

blocks.label: Horizontal Pull

exercises.name: BB Row
exercises.cue: This has been stuck at 165 lb since May because it always came fifth, when you were already cooked. It now leads the day, so it should move. Hinge forward until your chest is roughly parallel to the floor, knees slightly bent, back flat. Breathe in and brace. Pull the bar to your belly button by driving your ELBOWS backward past your ribs, then lower it all the way under control. Your torso does not move: if you are standing up a little to help the bar, it is too heavy.

alts.name: Lat Pulldown
alts.cue: Sit tall with your thighs locked under the pad. Start with your arms fully straight so you feel the stretch down your sides. Pull your ELBOWS down toward your ribs rather than thinking about your hands, and bring the bar to your upper chest. Let it back up slowly and all the way straight. Building toward real pull-ups.

alts.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
alts.cue: This is your freestyle catch trained directly, which is why it stays even though the rest of the day changed. Cable set high, rope or straight bar, stand back a step and hinge slightly forward. Arms stay STRAIGHT the whole time, elbows barely bent and locked there. Sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs and squeeze the muscles down the sides of your back, then let it float back up. Much lighter than a lat pulldown, because straight arms are a long lever.

alts.name: Chest-Supported DB Row
alts.cue: Chest on an incline bench, dumbbells hanging. The bench removes the lower back entirely, so nothing can cheat. Good on a day the RDLs left your back tired.

alts.name: Seated Cable Row
alts.cue: Tall chest, pull the handle to your stomach, squeeze the shoulder blades, let it stretch all the way forward.

alts.name: DB Pullover
alts.cue: Lying across or along a bench, one dumbbell held over the chest with near-straight arms. Lower it behind your head until you feel the stretch under the armpits, then pull it back over. 3x12.

alts.name: Assisted Pull-Up
alts.cue: Set the counterweight so you get 6 clean reps: full hang with straight arms at the bottom, chin over the bar at the top. Log the COUNTERWEIGHT, and remember it is the one number here that should go DOWN over time. When 6 feels easy, take 10 lb of assistance off.

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
exercises.cue: Hang from the pull-up bar on top of the rack, arms straight, feet clear of the floor. Bring both knees up toward your chest, and at the top KEEP GOING for a couple of inches by curling your hips under you, as if you were trying to show someone the soles of your shoes. That last bit is the part your abdominals actually do: stopping when your thighs are level is hip work and they only hold on. Then lower under control until your legs are straight and you have come to a STOP before the next rep, so every one starts from still rather than from a swing. Success looks like: no swinging, and you feel it across the front of your stomach at the top rather than in the front of your hips the whole way. If you cannot stop the swing, do fewer reps. Ten a set, and when fifteen is easy, straighten the legs instead of adding weight. THIS CUE IS A DRAFT: nobody has read it standing at the bar. Use the note box and say what it should say.
exercises.whyHere: Hanging knee raises go in the row rest on your own ruling: the bar is on top of the rack you are already standing in, and you said you would rather hang than lie on the floor.

alts.name: Hollow Hold
alts.cue: Lower back pressed flat into the floor, arms overhead and legs straight and lifted, so your body makes a shallow banana. Bend the knees or keep arms at your sides if the back lifts. 3x20s.

blocks.why: Rowing is the only movement in the week that trains the muscles between your shoulder blades as the prime mover rather than as helpers, so it gets two sessions, and this is the heavier one. Hanging knee raises go in the row rest on your own ruling: the bar is on top of the rack you are already standing in, and you said you would rather hang than lie on the floor.

blocks.label: Lower Back

exercises.name: Lumbar Extension
exercises.cue: NEW, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT EXERCISE FROM THE ONE YOU HAVE BEEN DOING ON THIS MACHINE. Same frame, opposite instruction. On the back extension you have logged since June you hold your back FLAT and your hip does the moving. Here your hip stays put and your BACK does the moving. That is the only way anything in your gym trains the muscles either side of your spine as the thing that moves you rather than the thing that holds on. START WITH NO WEIGHT AT ALL, arms crossed on your chest, and do not add any until this is easy: the weights on your other back extension do not carry over, and starting there is how people hurt themselves on this. HOW TO SET UP. Same as the other one. Hip pad top edge just below your hip bones, ankles under the rollers, feet flat. HOW TO DO IT. Start standing tall in the frame. Let your upper back curl down first, then your middle back, then your lower back, one bit at a time, the way you would roll down a wall. Three seconds down, and only as far as is comfortable, which the first few times will be about half the range. Then reverse it: lower back first, then middle, then upper, until you are standing tall again. STOP AT TALL. Do not arch backwards past it. Success looks like: the work is low down, in a band across your waist, and the next day feels like a working ache rather than anything sharp. Ten to fifteen reps. STOP AND TELL ME if you get anything sharp, anything that shoots down a leg, or anything still there the next morning. This one is a draft written for you and you are the only person who can say whether it works, so use the note box under it after the first session either way.

alts.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
alts.cue: THIS IS HIP WORK, NOT LOWER-BACK WORK, and that is a correction to what this card used to imply. With your back held flat, the muscles that MOVE you here are your bum and the back of your thighs. Your lower back holds still, which is exactly what it does in a squat or a Romanian deadlift. Nothing in your gym trains the lower back as the muscle that moves, and there is a question about that on this exercise. HOW TO SET UP. The padded frame angled at about 45 degrees. Set the hip pad so its TOP EDGE sits just below your hip bones, on the top of your thigh, not on your belly. Too high and you cannot bend at the hip; too low and it digs in. Ankles under the two rollers, feet flat on the platform. Hug the dumbbell against your chest with both arms. HOW TO DO IT. Bend forward at the HIP, letting your upper body fold down toward the floor, until you feel a stretch down the back of your thighs. Keep your back FLAT the whole way, like a plank, never rounded into a C. Then squeeze your bum and drive back up until your body is one straight line from ankle to head, and STOP THERE. Do not carry on past straight into an arch. Two seconds down, one second up. Success looks like: your back never changes shape, and you feel it in your bum and the back of your thighs. If you feel a pinch in your lower back instead of a working ache in the bum, you either rounded on the way down or went past straight at the top. YOUR WEIGHTS SO FAR: 40 lb in June, 45 in July, 3x10 at 50 lb on 8 August. TEN TO FIFTEEN REPS, and go up 5 lb once you hit fifteen. The range is that wide on purpose: at ten to twelve, the next dumbbell up is a bigger jump than twelve good reps earns, so you would fail it and drop back every time.

alts.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
alts.cue: On the floor. Lie on your back, one heel planted close to your butt, the other leg lifted and held straight out. Push through the planted heel and lift your hips until your body is a straight line from knee to shoulder, then lower slowly. Success looks like: you feel it in the back of the planted thigh and the butt cheek, not in your lower back. If you feel your lower back, your hips went too high. 3x12 each side.

exercises.name: DB Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.cue: Standing, one dumbbell held in both hands behind your head, elbows pointing up and staying pointed up. Straighten your arms to lift the weight overhead without letting your elbows drift out sideways. Lower until you feel a stretch under the arm. Success looks like: your elbows stay in the same place the whole set and only your forearms move. If your elbows flare, go lighter.
exercises.whyHere: The tricep extension goes in the rest because the arms take no part in a back extension.

open.q: You said you'd rather do assisted dips than tricep pushdowns. Two catches. Your triceps get 4 sets a week and that is the least that still builds them, so the dip has to be added on top, not swapped in. And the dip has its own machine, so this part of the session becomes two stops instead of one. Still want it?

alts.cue: Cable high, rope or straight bar. Pin your elbows to your sides and keep them there: only the forearms move. Push down until the arms are completely straight, hold half a second, then let it come up slowly until you feel the stretch. If your elbows drift forward or you lean over the bar, drop the weight.

Success looks like: your elbows stay the same distance apart the whole time and your ribs do not flare forward. If your back arches, go lighter. alts.name: DB Skullcrusher
alts.cue: Lying on a bench, a dumbbell in each hand, bend at the elbow to lower them beside your ears and press back up. Use this if overhead bothers your shoulder.

alts.name: EZ Bar Skullcrusher

tuesday.name: Session B
tuesday.title: Session B: pull fresh, hinge heavy

blocks.label: Vertical Pull, then Crunch

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Sit tall with your thighs locked under the pad. Start with your arms fully straight so you feel the stretch down your sides. Pull your ELBOWS down toward your ribs rather than thinking about your hands, and bring the bar to your upper chest. Let it back up slowly and all the way straight. Building toward real pull-ups.

alts.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
alts.cue: This is your freestyle catch trained directly, which is why it stays even though the rest of the day changed. Cable set high, rope or straight bar, stand back a step and hinge slightly forward. Arms stay STRAIGHT the whole time, elbows barely bent and locked there. Sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs and squeeze the muscles down the sides of your back, then let it float back up. Much lighter than a lat pulldown, because straight arms are a long lever.

alts.name: Assisted Pull-Up
alts.cue: Set the counterweight so you get 6 clean reps: full hang with straight arms at the bottom, chin over the bar at the top. Log the COUNTERWEIGHT, and remember it is the one number here that should go DOWN over time. When 6 feels easy, take 10 lb of assistance off.

alts.name: DB Pullover
alts.cue: Lying across or along a bench, one dumbbell held over the chest with near-straight arms. Lower it behind your head until you feel the stretch under the armpits, then pull it back over. 3x12.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
exercises.cue: Kneel facing the pulldown machine with the rope at the top. Hold the rope beside your ears and let your elbows stay there the whole set: the arms do not pull. Curl your ribs down towards your hips so your back rounds, then come back up slowly. Success looks like: the movement happens between your ribs and your hips and nowhere else. If your hips are folding and your back stays flat, you are doing a hip hinge on your knees, not a crunch. Start light enough that you can do it slowly.
exercises.whyHere: the only loadable trunk exercise in the week, and it is done IN TURN rather than in the rest, because both hang off the same high pulley and the attachment has to change between them

alts.name: DB Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. A dumbbell in each hand. Push your hips back and lean your chest forward to about 45 degrees, roughly halfway to parallel with the floor, back flat, eyes down. Let the dumbbells hang straight below your chest with a small bend in the elbows. Now open your arms out to the SIDES like opening a pair of curtains, until your hands are level with your shoulders. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly. Success looks like: your torso does not rise as you lift, and you feel it between the shoulder blades rather than in your lower back. Go light, this is a small muscle. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.
alts.whyHere: The reverse fly goes in the pulldown rest because it works the back of the shoulder, which the pulldown does not train as a prime mover.

alts.name: Cable Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. At the adjustable cable column, standing tall, a handle in each hand and a small bend in the elbows. Now open your arms out to the SIDES like opening a pair of curtains, until your hands are level with your shoulders. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly. Success looks like: your torso does not rise as you lift, and you feel it between the shoulder blades rather than in your lower back. Go light, this is a small muscle. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.

alts.name: Chest-Supported Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Same movement lying face down on an incline bench, which removes the lower back entirely. Use this if the standing version makes your back ache.

alts.name: Cable Pallof Press
alts.cue: Cable at chest height, stand side-on, both hands on the handle at your chest. Press it straight out and refuse to let it twist you. Hold two seconds at full reach.

blocks.why: Pulling down from overhead and rowing toward you are different jobs at the shoulder: one brings the arm down to your side, the other pulls the elbow back behind you. This one leads so it is done fresh at least once a week. What follows it is the only loadable trunk exercise in the week, and it is done IN TURN rather than in the rest, because both hang off the same high pulley and the attachment has to change between them.

blocks.label: Main Lift: Romanian Deadlift

exercises.name: BB Romanian Deadlift
exercises.cue: The heavy hinge, the one we progress. Breathe IN and tighten your stomach. Bar stays touching your legs the whole way, shins vertical. Bend the knees slightly and then FREEZE them, then push your hips backward toward the wall behind you. Go down until you feel a strong stretch down the back of your thighs, usually around knee height, and no further. Squeeze your bum and snap the hips forward to stand up, breathing out at the top. If your lower back rounds you have gone too far down. STRAPS, because you asked on 18 August: yes, use them, and they will not cost you anything here. Do the first warm-up set with bare hands so you keep noticing what your grip is doing, then strap up for all four working sets. The hamstrings are what this lift is for, and stopping a set because the bar is slipping out of your fingers trains neither. Your grip is not being neglected either: the Farmer Carry on Friday and the Suitcase Carry on Monday are both held bare-handed and that is where grip is meant to be worked. This is standard coaching practice rather than something a trial has tested, so it is a convention, not evidence.

alts.name: Single-Leg RDL
alts.cue: Has sat at 40 lb since May, so this time the weight moves, not just the reps. One dumbbell in the hand OPPOSITE the standing leg. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent and frozen. Push the hip backward and let the free leg extend straight behind you like a see-saw, keeping your hips square to the floor: the back hip must not open toward the ceiling. Go until you feel the hamstring stretch, then stand and squeeze. Slow. Touch the bench with your free toe if you lose balance.

alts.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
alts.cue: On the 45 degree pad. Hinge down and squeeze your bum to come up. Hug a plate for load.

alts.name: DB Romanian Deadlift
alts.cue: Two heavy dumbbells in front of your thighs. Same hip push backward, same freeze in the knees.

alts.name: KB Swing
alts.cue: Same hip snap, done fast. Hike the bell back between your legs, then SNAP the hips forward so the bell floats to chest height. Arms do nothing. Start at 35 lb. 2x12.

alts.name: Smith RDL
alts.cue: Bar on rails so it cannot drift away from your legs. Useful for grooving the hinge when you are tired.

alts.name: B-Stance RDL
alts.cue: Back toe lightly touching the floor for balance, but almost all the weight on the front leg. Much easier to balance, so you can load it heavier.

exercises.name: DB Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. A dumbbell in each hand hanging at your sides, palms facing your thighs, a small bend kept in the elbows. Lift both arms out SIDEWAYS, not forward, until your hands are level with your shoulders and no higher. Lead with the elbows, as if you were pouring from two jugs. Lower slowly, about twice as long coming down as going up. Success looks like: your shoulders do not rise toward your ears, and you can stop the weight dead at the top instead of it swinging. If either fails, go lighter. This is the SIDE of the shoulder, and it is the one thing nothing else in the week trains: every press works the front, every row works the back. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.
exercises.whyHere: The lateral raise goes in the rest because the shoulder takes no part in a hinge.

alts.name: KB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same movement with the lightest kettlebells, held by the handle. Use them if the light dumbbells are gone.

alts.name: Seated DB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same raise, sitting on the end of a bench. Sitting stops you swinging, so use it if the standing version keeps turning into a heave.

blocks.why: The heavy hinge, second in the session so it still gets a fresh slot. Six to eight reps, which are the rep counts you actually perform on it. This is one of only three hamstring exposures in the week, so it is not a lift to skip. The lateral raise goes in the rest because the shoulder takes no part in a hinge.

blocks.label: Horizontal Press: Bench

exercises.name: BB Bench Press
exercises.cue: Flat bench inside the rack, safety pins set at chest height BEFORE you load the bar, every time, because you train alone. Lie down and set your feet flat. Grip a little wider than your shoulders. Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the bench and keep them there the whole set: that is what protects the shoulder. Lower the bar to your lower chest under control until it touches lightly, then press it back up. Success looks like: the bar touches the same spot every rep and your shoulder blades never come unstuck. If you have to bounce it off your chest, it is too heavy.

alts.name: Front Squat
alts.cue: Your second squat of the week, deliberately light. This is the technique fix: because the bar sits on the FRONT of your shoulders, your body is forced upright and depth gets easier, which is exactly what a back squat struggles with. Bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows driven forward and UP so the upper arms are near parallel to the floor. Let your fingertips just hook under the bar, the shoulders hold it, not the hands. Sit straight down, elbows stay high the whole time. If the elbows drop, the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: BB Back Squat
alts.cue: The lift we are progressing. Stance slightly wider than your hips with the toes turned out a little. Breathe IN and hold it, tighten your stomach like you are about to be poked, then sit down between your feet until the crease of your hip is below the top of your knee. Knees push out over your second toe, they do not fall inward. Stand up and breathe out at the top. Take a fresh breath and re-tighten before EVERY rep, not just the first.

alts.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
alts.cue: Same upright effect with a dumbbell held at the chest, and no wrist or elbow demand at all. The easiest way to feel a deep upright squat.

alts.name: Leg Press
alts.cue: Feet shoulder width on the platform. Lower until your knees are near your chest without your lower back rounding off the pad, then press. Use this on a day your back is tired.

alts.name: Smith Squat
alts.cue: On rails. Feet slightly forward of the bar. Same depth, no balance demand.

exercises.name: DB Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.cue: Standing, one dumbbell held in both hands behind your head, elbows pointing up and staying pointed up. Straighten your arms to lift the weight overhead without letting your elbows drift out sideways. Lower until you feel a stretch under the arm. Success looks like: your elbows stay in the same place the whole set and only your forearms move. If your elbows flare, go lighter.
exercises.whyHere: The tricep extension goes in the rest because the triceps assist the press and this is the only movement in the week where they are the prime mover.

alts.name: Tricep Pushdown
alts.cue: Cable high, rope or straight bar. Pin your elbows to your sides and keep them there: only the forearms move. Push down until the arms are completely straight, hold half a second, then let it come up slowly until you feel the stretch. If your elbows drift forward or you lean over the bar, drop the weight.

alts.name: Cable Overhead Tricep Extension
alts.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. At the high pulley. Take the handle overhead, then bend only your elbows to lower it behind your head until you feel a stretch down the back of your arms, about level with the base of your skull. Your upper arms stay pointing at the ceiling and DO NOT drift forward: that is the whole exercise. Straighten the arms to come back up. Success looks like: your elbows stay the same distance apart the whole time and your ribs do not flare forward. If your back arches, go lighter. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.

alts.name: DB Skullcrusher
alts.cue: Lying on a bench, a dumbbell in each hand, bend at the elbow to lower them beside your ears and press back up. Use this if overhead bothers your shoulder.

alts.name: EZ Bar Skullcrusher
alts.cue: Lying on a bench with the EZ bar. Keep the upper arms still and pointing at the ceiling, bend only at the elbow to lower the bar toward your forehead, then straighten. Light.

It leads here so it happens fresh. The tricep extension goes in the rest because the triceps assist the press and this is the only movement in the week where they are the prime mover.

exercises.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides. Put the top of your back foot on the bench, laces down. Your front foot should be far enough forward that at the bottom your front shin is straight up and down, not leaning forward over your toes. Lower until your back knee is close to the floor. Drive up through the FRONT heel. The back leg is a kickstand, it does not push.

If the elbows drop, the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up. Stepping backward rather than forward keeps the load off the front knee.

alts.name: Walking Lunge
alts.cue: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.

alts.name: Cossack Squat
alts.cue: The deeper version. Same sideways sit, but let the straight leg's toes come up and go as low as you can. Bodyweight first, hold a dumbbell at the chest when it is easy. 3x6/side.

alts.name: DB Step-Up
alts.cue: Bench at knee height, drive through the heel of the top foot. 8/leg.

exercises.name: DB Calf Raise
exercises.cue: Standing on the floor in the rest between lunge sets, a dumbbell in each hand hanging at your sides. Feet about hip width. Push all the way up onto your toes, as high as you can go, and hold for one second at the top. Then lower slowly, about three seconds down, until your heels touch the floor and you feel a stretch through the back of the calf. Success looks like: you can hold the top position still for a second without wobbling, and the slow way down is what you feel most. If you cannot hold the top, the dumbbells are too heavy. This is the flat-floor version, so the stretch at the bottom is smaller than on the machine; that is the trade for it costing you no walk.

alts.name: Machine Calf Raise
alts.cue: On the standing calf machine. Let the heels sink until you feel a stretch, pause one second at the bottom, then push all the way up onto your toes and squeeze for one second. Slow both directions. This is ankle insurance for the running.

blocks.why: One leg at a time, eight to fourteen reps a leg. Nothing else in the week trains the calf as a prime mover, and it goes in the rest here because the calf takes no part in a split squat and you can do it standing right where you are.

blocks.label: Horizontal Press

exercises.name: Chest Fly Machine
exercises.cue: Elbows slightly bent and fixed, bring the arms together in front of you and squeeze for one second. Stretch, not a press.

alts.name: DB Incline Press
alts.cue: SET THE BENCH ONE OR TWO NOTCHES UP FROM FLAT, about 30 degrees, not half way up. This is what you have been doing since at least 28 August and the card was still saying flat, so your logged weights come with you and nothing resets. THE DIFFERENCE, since you asked in the note box: neither one is better. Flat works the middle and lower chest, an incline works the top of the chest and more front shoulder, and they are two halves of the same muscle. The steeper you go the more the shoulder takes over, which is why one or two notches and no more. Success looks like: you feel it across your collarbone rather than under your nipple line. If the shoulders are doing all of it, drop the bench a notch. Feet flat on the floor. Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the bench and keep them there, like you are pinching a pencil between them. Breathe in, lower the dumbbells until you feel a good stretch across the chest, PAUSE for one second so there is no bounce, then press up and breathe out. The dumbbells travel slightly toward each other at the top but do not clang. ADDED 2026-08-22, after he reported feeling this mostly in the triceps and the front of the shoulder: that is usually where the dumbbells are travelling, not how hard you are pushing. Two things to try. Before the first rep, pull your shoulder blades DOWN and TOGETHER into the bench and keep them pinned there the whole set, so your chest is the highest point and the shoulders cannot roll forward. Then press over your LOWER chest, not your collarbone: at the bottom the dumbbells should be beside your nipples with your elbows about halfway between tucked-in and straight-out, and at the top they finish above the same spot rather than drifting toward your face. Success looks like: at the bottom you feel a stretch across the chest, not a pinch at the front of the shoulder. This is standard coaching practice, not a trial finding.

alts.name: Machine Chest Press
alts.cue: Your second press of the week, moderate rather than heavy: Tuesday is the day the bench gets pushed. Machine on purpose, so a tired chest does not have to balance dumbbells. Set the seat so the handles line up with the MIDDLE of your chest. Press out until the arms are straight without locking hard, then come back slowly until you feel the stretch. Shoulder blades stay pinned back against the pad.

alts.name: Assisted Dip
alts.cue: Lean your chest forward to bias the chest. Enough counterweight for 8 clean reps. You had 5 strict dips in May, so this is trackable.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.cue: Done after the curls rather than alternating with them, because it needs room to walk and the preacher seat does not travel. A heavy dumbbell in each hand, stand as tall as you can, shoulders back, stomach tight, and walk for the seconds shown. Grip, posture and everything down your sides at once. Put them down before your form falls apart, not after. COUNT SECONDS, and type the seconds. Start the watch before you pick the dumbbells up, because you cannot press anything with both hands full. Get to the top of the range on time first, then go heavier.
exercises.whyHere: the carry goes in the press rest: it trains the grip, which pressing does not

alts.name: DB Static Hold
alts.cue: Heavy dumbbells held at your sides, standing still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this when the floor is too crowded to walk.

alts.name: KB Farmer Carry
alts.cue: Kettlebells instead, and THE RACK STOPS AT 50 LB EACH: that is the whole set, 20 up to 50, two of each. His note #18, 2026-08-25: 'Therea no kettlebell after 50 for farmers'. He is right, and it is why the prescribed version is dumbbells, which go to 90 and which he has already carried at 75 per hand. Use this one when the dumbbells are taken, not when you want it heavier. They hang differently and swing a little, so the grip works harder at the same weight.

alts.name: KB Suitcase Hold
alts.cue: One kettlebell in one hand, stand still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this if the floor is too crowded to walk.

alts.name: Suitcase Carry
alts.cue: One dumbbell only. Much harder on the side you are NOT carrying, because it has to stop you leaning. Swap hands each set.

blocks.why: The chest and the lats are the two muscles here that get no helper credit from anything at all, which is why both are expensive to cover and why both used to sit at the bottom of the week. Nothing else asks the hands to hold on for forty seconds, so the carry goes in the press rest: it trains the grip, which pressing does not. THIS IS THE BLOCK TO DROP IF THE CLOCK BEATS YOU, and the price is that the grip falls from six sets a week to three, under the floor of four.
